name: Chulalongkorn
summary: Chulalongkorn pursued gradual abolition of slavery and corvée, centralized administration and modern public infrastructure while preserving royal authority. He adapted foreign institutions selectively and negotiated territorial concessions to protect Siam’s independence. His reforms also brought Buddhist administration more closely under the state.

notes:
Reviewed the full reign, abolition, prostration reform, royal absolutism, treatment of critics, centralization, education, Buddhist institutions, modern infrastructure and territorial diplomacy. The Waseda dissertation was downloaded in full and searched, including its quotations of the 1885 reply and 1888 and 1903 royal explanations; these remain secondhand evidence at medium or low confidence. The abolition law is attributed because his personal authorship of the policy is independently documented. Ordinary laws and successors’ policies were not treated as his positions. Targeted ecology research located forestry changes but did not establish personal positions matching the environmental statements. All remaining nulls reviewed against the complete statement list. No inferred answers. Auditor identification: the runtime identifies this assistant as GPT-6/Codex but does not expose an exact version or variant; gpt-6 is the available identifier, not an asserted variant.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 10 answers taken from it, 12 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass built on his own texts: the 1888 speech (read in full, Thai), the 1905 Slavery and Conscription Acts, the 1897 Local Administration Act, the 1902 Sangha Act and the 1899 sakdina act, plus Engel's study for his 1885-87 reply, councils, courts and provinces. Absolute monarch, so acts he personally drove count; the 1897 and 1902 acts are drafted by others in his name, so those answers are medium at most. Searched all themes; economy, society, ecology, technology, culture and most of world have no own-words record (his letters 'Klai Ban' exist only as garbled OCR; the Waseda dissertation used by the first audit was offline), so they are null. First audit answers on preserve-national-culture, tech-with-ancestral-values, no-land-for-peace, suppress-opposition and state-directs-investment rest on secondary summaries and were not re-found in his own words.
